explanation: 出口 (deguchi) means “exit” — 出 (go out) + 口 (mouth/opening). Its opposite, 入口 (iriguchi), means entrance.
hint: Look at the first kanji: 出 means 'to go out'. Where does the door lead?
source: Unschool Academy original practice item, drafted against the Japan Foundation JFT-Basic official test structure (https://www.jpf.go.jp/jft-basic/e/about/index.html). Draft — pending Japanese SME review.
stem: You see this sign at a station: 出口. What does it mean?

explanation: 火曜日 (kayoubi) is Tuesday — 火 (fire) is the day-marker. 出してください = “please put out”. Apartment notices like this are classic JFT everyday-reading material.
hint: Match the kanji 火曜 to the weekday name you already know.
source: Unschool Academy original practice item, drafted against the Japan Foundation JFT-Basic official test structure (https://www.jpf.go.jp/jft-basic/e/about/index.html). Draft — pending Japanese SME review.
stem: A notice at your apartment says: ゴミは 火曜日に 出してください. When do you put out the rubbish?
